title: Product kernel of Tanimoto and RBF on descriptors
spec: Build a second kernel from the RDKit descriptor matrix. Standardize desc_features with training-set mean and std, clip to [-5, 5], and compute an RBF kernel exp(-||x-x'||^2 / (2*d)), where d is the number of descriptors. Use the elementwise product K_tanimoto * K_rbf as the GP kernel and choose sigma2 with the existing grouped CV loop. A molecule then counts as similar only when both its substructure fingerprint and its physchem profile agree. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.

title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP
spec: Replace the single fingerprint with a choice among three configurations: radius 1 with 1024 bits, radius 2 with 2048 bits (current), and radius 3 with 4096 bits. Pick the configuration by the same grouped 5-fold Spearman criterion already used for sigma2, jointly over the (configuration, sigma2) pairs, inside fit_predict on training data only. Use the chosen configuration for the test predictions. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged. The selection stays within training data, so no test leakage occurs.

title: Gaussian process with a kNN-based prior mean
spec: In gp_mean, replace the constant prior mean mu = y.mean() with a local prior: for each test molecule, use the mean target of its k=10 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules (computed from the same K matrices). For the GP fit, the training prior is the leave-self-out kNN mean within the training set. Keep the GP posterior as a residual correction: pred = prior + K_te @ alpha, where alpha solves (K_tr + sigma2 I) alpha = y - prior_tr. Keep sigma2 selection by grouped CV as it is now.

title: Inner-grouped-CV stopping round for the descriptor LightGBM
spec: Before the final descriptor fit, run GroupKFold(5) on the training set with Murcko scaffold groups and train the descriptor LightGBM once per fold with 1000 boosting rounds at learning rate 0.03. Record the mean Spearman of the out-of-fold predictions at each of the rounds 100, 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000 using predict with num_iteration. Use the best round count for the final fit on all training molecules. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged, and the search is over stopping points only.

title: Residual GP on top of descriptor LightGBM
spec: Turn the fingerprint GP into a residual model. Inside fit_predict, first compute out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training molecules using GroupKFold(5) with Murcko scaffold groups, so the residuals are honest. Set r = y - oof, where y is the rank-transformed target. Fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (existing gp_mean and choose_sigma2 applied to r, with the same sigma2 grid) and predict residuals for the test molecules. The fingerprint-side prediction is the full LightGBM test prediction (trained on all training data) plus the GP residual prediction. Rank-blend this combined score with the existing LightGBM rank at weight 0.5 each, and keep seed handling unchanged.

title: Huber-robust GP via iteratively reweighted noise
spec: Make the GP noise term per-sample. Start with weights w_i = 1 and sigma2_i = sigma2 / w_i. Solve (K + diag(sigma2_i)) alpha = y - mu, compute the residuals r_i = y_i minus the training fitted value, and set w_i = min(1, c / |r_i|) with c = 1.345 times the median absolute residual. Iterate three times. Predictions use the final alpha. This down-weights training molecules whose labels disagree with their Tanimoto neighbours, using a Huber rule, and leaves the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

title: Gaussian-rank (normal-score) target transform
spec: Replace the target line y = rankdata(train_y)/len(train_y) with normal scores: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)). Ranks are unchanged, so the Spearman ordering of the training labels is preserved, but the spacing of the regression target becomes Gaussian. Both the LightGBM fit and the GP mean are then fit on this target, and the final blend still uses rankdata on the predictions. This is a single-line change.

title: Residualised target on a lipophilicity linear baseline
spec: Before fitting, regress the rank target on two physchem columns, Crippen MolLogP and TPSA, with an ordinary least-squares fit on the training set, using an intercept. Use the residuals as the new target for the descriptor LightGBM and for the GP (centre the GP targets as before). At prediction time add the linear baseline back to the model predictions for test molecules, then rank-blend as before. This is a target change that lets the models focus on structure beyond logP and TPSA.
